description: Formal specification for the 6 canonical hypotheses testing the interaction between resource endowments, institutional dynamics, and bandit algorithm performance.

hypotheses.name: Resource Curse Effect
hypotheses.description: Resource-rich sites attract disproportionate early investment but end up with higher extraction and lower long-run population.

hypotheses.name: Institutional Quality Matters
hypotheses.description: Sites with better initial institutions achieve higher long-run populations, even when resource-poor.

hypotheses.name: Network Effects and Openness
hypotheses.description: Open, trade-oriented city clusters outperform isolated settlements, and the cluster premium increases with network scale.

hypotheses.name: Algorithm Comparison
hypotheses.description: Thompson Sampling and Whittle Index outperform UCB1 and epsilon-greedy in cumulative reward, especially in non-stationary scenarios.

hypotheses.name: Zipf's Law Emergence
hypotheses.description: At least one scenario produces a rank-size distribution approximating Zipf's law (slope ≈ -1.0).

hypotheses.name: UCB Bait Trap
hypotheses.description: UCB1 is disproportionately attracted to the boomtown during the collapse window; greedy baselines may be worse over the full horizon.
